fields.Front: Magnitude of the resultant of a distributed load \(w(x)\)
fields.Back: \(F_R=\displaystyle\int_L w(x)\,dx\): the area under the load curve
fields.SpeakFront: magnitude of the resultant of a distributed load w of x
fields.SpeakBack: the integral of w of x over the length; the area under the load curve
fields.Elaboration: Units: w in N/m, so the area is in N.

fields.Front: Where does the resultant of a distributed load act?
fields.Back: At \(\bar x=\dfrac{\int x\,w\,dx}{\int w\,dx}\): through the centroid of the load area
fields.SpeakFront: where does the resultant of a distributed load act?
fields.SpeakBack: at x bar equals the integral of x w d x over the integral of w d x; through the centroid of the load area
fields.Elaboration: Comes from matching moments: \(\bar xF_R=\int xw\,dx\). Uniform load: midpoint. Triangular: 1/3 from the heavy end.

golden.note: The uniform and triangular cases in Elaboration are derivable checks, not new facts.

fields.Elaboration: A particle needs only \(\sum\vec F=0\): concurrent forces produce no moment.
fields.Front: Equilibrium conditions for a rigid body
fields.SpeakBack: the sum of forces and the sum of moments about any point are both zero
fields.SpeakFront: equilibrium conditions for a rigid body

golden.note: Revision: the particle comparison moves to Elaboration. A contrast card only earns its place when both sides are already known on their own.

fields.Front: How many independent scalar equilibrium equations does a 2D rigid body give, and which?
fields.SpeakFront: how many independent scalar equilibrium equations does a two D rigid body give, and which?
fields.SpeakBack: three: sum of F x, sum of F y, and sum of moments about a point, each zero
fields.Elaboration: So one FBD can solve at most 3 unknowns. Taking moments about a point where unknowns meet removes them.

golden.note: The count is the recall target. The equations are a three-item list, but they're one coherent statement, not a set to memorize.

fields.Back: One force, normal to the surface the roller sits on
fields.SpeakFront: reactions at a roller support, in two D
fields.SpeakBack: one force, normal to the surface the roller sits on
fields.Elaboration: It only prevents motion into the surface.

golden.note: One card per support type instead of 'list the support types' (canon 13).

fields.Front: Reactions at a smooth pin or hinge (2D)
fields.Back: Two force components, \(F_x\) and \(F_y\); no moment
fields.SpeakFront: reactions at a smooth pin or hinge, in two D
fields.SpeakBack: two force components, F x and F y, and no moment
fields.Elaboration: It stops translation in both directions but lets the member rotate.

fields.SpeakFront: reactions at a fixed support, in two D
fields.SpeakBack: F x, F y, and a couple moment M
fields.Elaboration: It stops both translation and rotation.

golden.note: The three support cards interfere by design. The type name in each prompt is the distinguishing cue.

fields.Front: Why does a fixed support develop a moment reaction while a pin doesn't?
fields.Back: A support develops a couple moment only where it prevents rotation. A pin lets the member rotate; a fixed support doesn't.
fields.SpeakFront: why does a fixed support develop a moment reaction, while a pin does not?
fields.SpeakBack: a support only develops a couple moment where it prevents rotation; a pin lets the member rotate, a fixed support does not
fields.Elaboration: The general rule (slide 10 notes): a reaction force wherever translation is prevented, a couple moment wherever rotation is prevented, each in the opposite direction.

golden.note: The handwritten general rule becomes a why-card. The support cards become consequences of one principle, not three facts to memorize.

fields.Back: A member loaded at only two points, with its weight neglected, e.g. a link pinned at both ends
fields.SpeakFront: definition of a two force member
fields.SpeakBack: a member loaded at only two points, with its weight neglected, such as a link pinned at both ends

golden.note: The 'on exam' mark raises priority (canon 10: exam-flagged). One of three angles on this concept.

fields.Front: Direction of the forces in a two-force member
fields.Back: Equal, opposite, and along the line joining the two load points A and B
fields.SpeakFront: direction of the forces in a two force member
fields.SpeakBack: equal and opposite, and along the line joining the two load points
fields.Elaboration: \(\sum\vec F=0\) makes them equal and opposite. \(\sum M_A=0\) then puts the line of action through B. It works even for a curved member.

golden.note: 'Even curved' is the trap the slide's curved figure is testing.

fields.Front: Equilibrium conditions for a rigid body, compared with a particle
fields.Back: Rigid body: \(\sum\vec F=0\) and \(\sum\vec M_O=0\). Particle: \(\sum\vec F=0\) only.
fields.SpeakFront: equilibrium conditions for a rigid body, compared with a particle
fields.SpeakBack: a rigid body needs the sum of forces and the sum of moments both zero; a particle needs only the sum of forces
fields.Elaboration: Concurrent forces on a particle produce no moment, so no rotation is possible.
